questions.question: The benchmark shows website reads take about 900 ms and classification about 3 ms. What should you optimise?
options: The classifier, because its loops look slow
questions.explanation: Even a perfect classifier would save a few milliseconds. The measurement points at website reads.

questions.question: Why does the test count calls instead of asserting a time limit?
options: Counting is more accurate than timing.
Timing tests are flaky on shared machines; the call count checks the cause of the speed-up reliably.
Python cannot measure time in tests.
questions.explanation: The behaviour that makes it faster, one read per company, is deterministic; milliseconds are not.

questions.question: Why does the cache not store failed lookups?
options: Failures are too big to store.
A temporary failure would otherwise be repeated for the rest of the run.
questions.explanation: Caching a failure turns one bad moment into many. Only successful pages are remembered.
